description: Tarek Bazrouk, 20, was charged with federal hate crimes over a series of assaults on Jewish victims in New York City between 2024 and 2025, including an attack on a man wearing an Israel Defense Forces sweatshirt.

A man repeatedly rammed his car into the entrance of Chabad-Lubavitch World Headquarters at 770 Eastern Parkway in Crown Heights during Yud Shvat. No injuries reported; suspect Dan Sohail, 36, was taken into custody. NYPD is investigating it as an antisemitic hate crime.

Ayman Mohamad Ghazali rammed a vehicle into Temple Israel and opened fire before dying by suicide; a security guard was struck by the vehicle and injured. The FBI determined the attack was a Hezbollah-inspired act of terrorism against the Jewish community, motivated by the deaths of the attacker’s relatives in an Israeli airstrike in Lebanon days earlier.

Larry Montes disrupted Shabbat services at Central Synagogue in Midtown East, striking a congregant and headbutting a security guard. He was arrested and charged with hate crimes and damage to religious property resulting in injury.
A vehicle displaying a Palestinian flag drove past a Hertfordshire synagogue while an occupant shook a fist toward congregants celebrating Simchat Torah.
Free Palestine graffiti was sprayed on a bridge in Golders Green, an area with a large Jewish community. CST classified it among the first antisemitic incidents following October 7.
Staff discovered the word Gaza spray-painted on a sign outside the Wiener Holocaust Library. Police recorded the vandalism as a hate crime.
A threatening letter containing anti-Zionist and Islamist-extremist rhetoric was sent to the headteacher of a Jewish school.
A Jewish customer in a barbershop overheard two customers endorse Hitler's persecution of Jews and express regret that Jews had survived.
A poster depicting a baby kidnapped by Hamas was defaced with two swastikas.
Leaflets promoting halal cat food and invoking an antisemitic trope about Jewish greed were distributed to homes across Greater Manchester.
A Jewish schoolboy was assaulted outside his school and forced to say Free Palestine. Police investigated the incident as a hate crime.

A man brandished a knife and fought with people at a kosher supermarket after demanding to know whether they supported Israel or Palestine. Police arrested him on suspicion of racially aggravated affray.
Antisemitic graffiti was sprayed on Hillel House, the Jewish student center serving the University of Leeds. Police investigated the vandalism.
A man and woman were assaulted on Swanage High Street by a man who allegedly made antisemitic comments. Neither victim sustained serious injuries, and police arrested a suspect.
A coordinated series of Goyim Defence League leaflets alleging that feminism was Jewish was distributed at multiple locations in northern Scotland.
A man kicked a visibly Jewish pedestrian from behind, blamed him for killing Palestinians and threatened to kill him if he approached.
A Dorset synagogue received an email threatening that the sender would arrive the next morning and shoot Jewish people one by one.
Three masked men kidnapped a Jewish music producer, assaulted him and handcuffed him to a radiator. The victim sustained extensive facial injuries, and three men were later sentenced.
A memorial to Jewish victims of terrorism was defaced in Hove. Sussex Police investigated the vandalism as a hate crime.
Graffiti in Norwich combined a Star of David with a swastika, directly comparing Jews with Nazis.
A hostage poster on Jewish-owned property was defaced with graffiti.
A Jewish pupil was repeatedly told by a classmate that he should be gassed and that conditions should return to the 1940s; the classmate also made Nazi salutes.
A man allegedly made a Nazi salute toward participants in a Stop the Hate counter-protest in Trafalgar Square. Police issued an appeal to identify him.
A Free Palestine sticker was placed on a public chanukiah.
A perpetrator wrote antisemitic graffiti stating that Jews were Nazis and scum on several north Manchester buildings, including a kosher restaurant and a synagogue.

A synagogue entrance in Golders Green was smeared with excrement in the first publicly dated incident of a series targeting Jewish premises. Police investigated the attacks as antisemitic criminal damage.
An antisemitic caricature was drawn on a building in London.
An attacker drove a car at people outside Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation and attacked worshippers with a knife during Yom Kippur. Two Jewish men died and three others sustained serious injuries.
A Jewish news outlet received an email invoking ritual-abuse allegations and threatening to ensure that the outlet and its ancestors suffered.
A man at a gym claimed that events were a Jewish fabrication and that Jews owned everything, then repeated the allegation to the manager.
Participants on a walking tour were handed a poetry book containing several explicitly antisemitic works.
A man allegedly acted aggressively outside a synagogue in Crumpsall. Police charged him with a racially aggravated public-order offense and criminal damage.
Tony Steer asked a man outside a Finchley cricket club whether he was Jewish and then punched him in the mouth. Steer was convicted of racially aggravated assault.
Graffiti comparing the Gaza war to the Holocaust and displaying a false casualty figure was written on a London wall.
The words HATE JEWS were written beneath a bridge in London.
Seven masked teenage boys charged bicycles toward a visibly Jewish couple, tried to seize their religious clothing and threw stones and branches at them.
At a workplace social event, a colleague praised Hitler, minimized the Holocaust and blamed Jews for terrorist attacks while speaking to a Jewish victim.
An antisemitic conspiracy theory was written on a public poster in London.
Tavius Jean-Charles shouted a death threat against Jews at a driver in Stamford Hill and smashed the passenger window of the moving car. He later pleaded guilty.
Attackers poured accelerant over four ambulances operated by Hatzola and set them on fire in a synagogue car park. The ambulances were destroyed and nearby residents were displaced.
Tavius Jean-Charles was heard near a synagogue saying Jewish schools should be blown up. Police arrested him, and he later pleaded guilty.
A picture of Hitler was attached to a public post in a Jewish area of London.
Boycott Israeli Goods stickers were placed on a Hatzola community ambulance in Stamford Hill.
An antisemitic slur was written on a slide in a children's play area in London.
A man on the London Underground noticed a father's kippah, shouted at his visibly Jewish family and threatened to kill the father, claiming he had killed Jews before.
An antisemitic joke based on a Jewish stereotype was posted on Facebook and reported to CST by a UK victim or witness.

Two masked suspects placed bottles containing suspected petrol beside windows at a Finchley synagogue and threw a brick at the building. Police treated the attempted arson as an antisemitic hate crime.
An arson attack caused minor damage at Kenton United Synagogue. No one was injured, and a teenager later pleaded guilty.
Two Jewish men were stabbed in Golders Green, including one outside a synagogue. Police treated the attack as terrorism and arrested the suspect.
Several UK Jewish organisations received a coordinated mass email celebrating the Golders Green knife attack and containing extensive antisemitic language.
Rocks were thrown at a Jewish community ambulance while it transported a patient in Edgware. Police arrested a man on suspicion of aggravated criminal damage.
Two men approached a Jewish man in Clapton Common, shouted antisemitic abuse and filmed the encounter for social media. Both pleaded guilty to aggravated harassment.
A man allegedly directed antisemitic abuse at Orthodox Jewish passengers on a bus traveling through Stamford Hill. Prosecutors charged him with aggravated harassment and threatening behavior.
Dylan Ossei walked through Enfield shouting threats at the Jewish community, assaulted a man and repeatedly asked whether he was Jewish. He pleaded guilty.
Syeda Khatun shouted antisemitic abuse at a mother and children outside a Jewish school, then struck a father and pulled his beard. She was convicted of aggravated assault and harassment.
An antisemitic obscenity and a swastika were scrawled on a London bus stop.
A swastika and an obscenity were sprayed on the fence of a Jewish residence in London.
An antisemitic conspiracy slogan alleging that all roads led to Jews was written on an anti-immigration banner in Glasgow.
A Jewish man and his three-year-old son were assaulted in Markfield Park while the attacker made threats toward them and the wider Jewish community. Neither required medical treatment.
A participant in a spontaneous anti-Israel gathering called a journalist part of the “Jewish press” and tore his hat from his head.
Unknown attackers threw two Molotov cocktails at the Kahal Adass Jisroel community complex; they missed the building and security personnel extinguished them.
A man wearing a kippah was threatened by a person who said he would rip the “little cap” from his head.
Two men threatened a group carrying Israeli flags with death and insulted them in Arabic.
At Munich Central Station, a man shouted through a megaphone that Israel was not a country, all land belonged to Palestine, and Jews were “devils and monsters.”.
“Free Palestine from Zionists!” with a Star of David and “Save Israel from Zionists” was written on a university restroom door.
A gathering displayed the Shoah-reversal slogan “One Holocaust does not justify another.”.
A group carrying Palestinian flags chanted “child murderer Israel” after a rally held in solidarity with Israel.
Demonstrators chanted “Khaybar, Khaybar, ya yahud,” a slogan RIAS identifies as a religiously framed call for violence against Jews.
“Israel die! NS now!” was written on a bridge.
Near an anti-Israel demonstration, a group of men subjected a woman to antisemitic and sexist abuse and threatened sexual violence after she rejected their chants.
A Star of David was painted on the door of a house where a Jewish woman lived.
“Free Palestine” was written on the apartment door of an Israeli woman.

Students made repeated antisemitic statements in class and on a playground, including that Jews controlled politics and profited from wars. Treat as one documented school episode, not one record per statement.
Students told a classmate that the classmate’s family in Israel would die and Israel would be destroyed. The report withholds the town; regional centroid is permitted.
A campus notice falsely blamed Israel for the Al-Ahli hospital blast and labeled it a “Holocaust.”.
After a person shared information about a fundraiser for Israeli civilians, an acquaintance sent an antisemitic WhatsApp response blaming Jews collectively.
A hostage poster was defaced with “Zionist propaganda.”.
A poster showing hostages kidnapped by Hamas was defaced with “All Jews lie.”.
An object was thrown at the window of a couple displaying an Israeli flag and Star of David, cracking the glass while someone was in the room.
A tram passenger blamed Jews collectively for Israeli politics and invoked the charge that Jews killed Jesus; another passenger who intervened was insulted.
Calls of “Free Palestine” twice interrupted a ceremony recounting the stories of Jewish students deported during the Shoah.
The Jewish community received a letter threatening another “Kristallnacht” in Freiburg.
A portrait of an Auschwitz survivor in a Buchenwald Memorial exhibition was pelted by an unknown person.
An anti-Israel demonstrator photographed a woman counter-protester and said the country would be free only when all Jews disappeared, then declared “I am an antisemite.”.
Students accused a Jewish classmate of defending an “Israeli terror state” and told him that “someone like him” should not be surprised by hostility.
A passerby at a November 9 memorial event directed antisemitic and sexist insults at a woman.
A gathering displayed a poster comparing Nazi extermination practices with Israeli military action and asking “Where’s the difference?”.
A wooden sign was marked with antisemitic and antigypsy football-related graffiti reading “Jews, Gypsies, Chemnitzer FC.”.
A man distributing antisemitic university flyers shouted “Zionists are murderers” when asked to stop; the flyer also blamed Zionists for Nazism.
A student called a teacher a “dirty Jew” and “Frau Hitler,” threatened her, and injured her by slamming a door. The town is withheld; use Saxony centroid.
Jewish student Lahav Shapira was repeatedly punched and kicked after leaving a bar, suffering facial fractures requiring surgery. A court later found an antisemitic motive.
An incendiary device was thrown at the Oldenburg synagogue, causing a fire that was extinguished without injuries.
A gunman fired at the Israeli Consulate General and Munich Documentation Centre on the anniversary of the 1972 Olympics attack; two people suffered blast trauma and police killed the attacker.
Two men restrained a Jewish schoolgirl on her way to school, threatened her and called her a “dirty Jew” before she escaped. RIAS says this occurred shortly before the synagogue arson.
A hiker confronted a woman whose bag read “Feminist Zionist,” compared Gaza to Auschwitz, pushed her and called her a Nazi.
A person threatened a man wearing an “I stand with Israel” patch that he would receive the same treatment as his “Jewish friends.”.

An institution received a letter calling Jews pigs, marking Netanyahu with a swastika and containing an unidentified powder. Use institution/victim location if regional report supplies it; otherwise Hesse centroid.
Two swastikas were painted beside the front door of a Jewish couple’s home.
A Star of David was painted on a house where a Jewish person lived.
Stolpersteine were stolen from five locations on the anniversary of the Hamas massacre. Treat as one coordinated series unless the five addresses and separate narratives are recovered.
“JEWS OUT” and a swastika were written on a railway platform.
“Judaism is criminality” was spray-painted in the pedestrian zone.
A taxi driver told a passenger that his daughter’s Jewish Israeli landlord charged high rent because he was Jewish.
About five teenage Hansa Rostock fans repeatedly sang the “subway song,” describing a rail line to Auschwitz aimed at opposing fans. Geocode Rostock or route centroid consistently.
Demonstrators carried signs equating Israel with Nazi perpetrators and portraits glorifying Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar. One gathering, not one record per sign.
A demonstration chanted “Khaibar, Khaibar, ya yahud” and “Labbaik ya Nasrallah,” invoking violence against Jews and praising Hezbollah’s leader.
At a “Stop the slaughter in Rafah” gathering, signs compared Israel to the Holocaust and a speaker legitimized Hamas’s October 7 violence.
At a Nakba Day gathering, a speaker denied that the Shoah met a narrowly stated definition of genocide while calling Israel a perpetrator.

Unknown people twice wrote “Jew” in large letters on the home of an Israeli family. The report describes two occurrences but lacks separate dates; keep as one repeated-target record unless dates are recovered.
A Jewish Afro-German family found antisemitic and racist slurs written on the wet windows of their car.

Around 40 masked people armed with axes, saws, crowbars and clubs stormed the Free University executive offices, dragged employees from rooms and left antisemitic graffiti and Hamas-style red triangles. Police investigated multiple offenses.
A university sit-in included claims that Jews rule and oppress the world, calls for an intifada and antisemitic songs.
At the following day’s sit-in, speakers denied Israel’s right to exist, compared it with Nazi Germany and defended the BDS campaign.
A university restroom was marked with “Fuck your German guilt—Zionism is fascism” and “From the river to the sea.”.
A lecture-hall table at Chemnitz University of Technology was marked with an antisemitic slogan about burning Jews for heat.
“Free Jews from Being” was written in a restroom at Berlin University of the Arts.
A student gave a Nazi salute in a school hallway and shouted an antisemitic obscenity on the anniversary of the Hamas attack.
A student called a classmate a “stupid Jew” during a lesson. Town withheld; regional centroid permitted.
A Jewish institution received an email threatening its recipients with death and invoking Rothschild and a Jewish world-control conspiracy.
A Jewish man received an Instagram message blaming him for alleged Israeli crimes and saying the sender hoped he would burn in hell.
Three men entered a Jewish-owned shop after seeing a Jewish newspaper in the window, filmed themselves and aggressively threatened to slaughter people while customers and staff were present.
Stickers stating “one holocaust does not justify another” were placed beside a memorial to a destroyed synagogue.
A woman wearing a keffiyeh confronted a pro-Israel vigil and physically attacked a participant after disputing the vigil’s message. Confirm full passage/page when converting.
A supervisor told a Jewish employee that threats against the synagogue were unsurprising “given what Israel is doing.”.
Landscaping workers noticed an Israeli flag at an apartment and made antisemitic remarks about its resident.
A sticker depicted a rat with a human face, “Judas” on its forehead and a money bag, hanging from a gallows.
A regional-train passenger shouted “Heil Hitler” and called for Syrians and Jews to be sent to gas chambers.
An AfD municipal politician allegedly told a resident objecting to the party’s booth that her behavior would put her in Buchenwald; the incident was reported to police.
A woman entered an Asian delicatessen and directed racist and antisemitic abuse at staff, including calling Jews child murderers.
During a confrontation at an International Women’s Day demonstration, youths tried to seize a woman’s Israeli flag and one made a sexually violent antisemitic remark.
Several men approached a woman recording a Hebrew voice message, subjected her to antisemitic sexual abuse and threatened rape.
A person in an apartment-building hallway shouted that all Jews and foreigners should be gassed.
“Jews out” and “Free racism” were found at an outdoor swimming pool. Town withheld; Saxony centroid permitted.
A passerby shouted an antisemitic obscenity at a gathering showing solidarity with Israel.
On a local train, a passenger said Muslims and Christians lived peacefully until Jews caused conflict.
A speaker opened a demonstration with an Islamic prayer and made antisemitic statements during her speech.
A man spat at a couple leaving a counter-rally to an antisemitic demonstration and shouted an antisemitic slur at them.
Participants in an anti-Israel demonstration threw bottles and stones at two counter-demonstrations.
Counter-protesters were pelted with eggs and pebbles from an anti-Israel gathering.
After invoking a right-wing extremist politician, a bar patron tried to pull the kippah from a Jewish guest’s head.
Right-wing counter-demonstrators threatened Christopher Street Day participants with gas chambers.
A sticker combined an Antifa logo and Palestinian flag with “Fuck your German guilt. Zionism is fascism.”.
A speaker at a “Monday walk” invoked the antisemitic Morgenthau Plan conspiracy and compared it with government policy.

A man attacked a visitor at the Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe and cut his throat; emergency surgery saved him. The assailant said he had gone there seeking Jews and was later sentenced to 13 years.
A man attacked a tram passenger wearing a Star of David, tried to drag him off the tram, attacked him again after they disembarked and tore the necklace from his neck.
Two strangers insulted a couple after seeing the man’s Star of David shirt, pursued them and shattered vehicle windows as the couple tried to leave, injuring them with glass.
A man shouted “Free Palestine” at a visibly identifiable rabbi shopping with his children, knocked the rabbi’s phone away and shoved him.
A group called a person a “Zionist pig,” punched and repeatedly beat them while blaming them for genocide; the victim required hospital treatment.
A man extinguished and threw away a memorial candle, then struck and choked a woman while she cleaned a Stolperstein.
An e-bike rider spat on a participant at a commemoration of the Nazi-era demolition of Nuremberg’s main synagogue.
A Jewish person was threatened with “your house will burn soon” and “you should all be burned.”.
A right-wing extremist rally participant told counter-protesters that he hoped they would be gassed and called them Jews.
The “Here and Now—To the Victims of the Nazi Judicial System” memorial was defaced with “Israel is the enemy of humanity” and “Fuck Israel.”.
The Jewish cemetery was marked with “SS” and “SA,” apparently shortly before Holocaust Remembrance Day.
A swastika was scratched into the iced windshield of a Jewish person’s parked car; the owner’s Jewish identity was known in the neighborhood.

Civil-society institutions working against antisemitism received an email asserting that Jews were “impure” and promoting antisemitic medical and psychological conspiracy claims. Regional centroid permitted.
“KILL JEWS” was found in the restroom of an intercity train traveling from Berlin toward Frankfurt. Geocode departure city or route midpoint consistently.
An antisemitic slur referring to “Jewish sewer rats” was written on a University of Duisburg-Essen campus wall.
“Fuck Jews!!” was written on a park bench.
An apartment-building mailbox was marked “ZIO PIGS DIE.”.
“Jüdde Eck” (“Jew Corner”) was written on a street sign near a synagogue.
A psychotherapist responded to a Jewish patient’s concern about antisemitism by invoking Israeli policy and the conspiracy myth that Jews control stock markets. The patient changed therapists.
A delivery driver pointed at visibly Jewish customers leaving a kosher shop, shouted “Jew” and “Free Palestine,” then assumed a fighting stance before shop employees intervened.
A demonstration included chants excluding “Zionists,” praised Hamas and its armed wing and called for death to the Israeli military. Treat as one gathering incident.
At a Holocaust Remembrance Day rally, a speaker invoked a Rothschild/Mossad conspiracy and referred disparagingly to Auschwitz remembrance.
At a far-right anti-CSD demonstration, speakers promoted a Jewish-world-conspiracy narrative using coded references to “puppet masters” destroying society.
A person called a visibly Jewish man wearing a kippah a “fucking Jew.”.
“Zionism is a death cult” was found as graffiti.
During a university event, a guest speaker denied the documented scale of sexual violence during the October 7 attack.
At a university event, an audience member questioned the six-million Jewish death toll immediately after the Shoah was mentioned.
A junction box was marked “Foreigners out,” a football-club abbreviation and a Star of David, using Jewish labeling to demean a rival team.
A far-right demonstration speaker promoted “remigration” through a “globalist agenda” conspiracy narrative that RIAS identifies with antisemitic Great Replacement ideology.
Antisemitic graffiti was found on Berlin's Block of Women memorial, which commemorates a protest by non-Jewish women against the detention of their Jewish relatives.
A shed at the home of Brandenburg antisemitism commissioner Andreas Büttner was set on fire and a red triangle was painted at the property. Büttner and his family were not injured.
